**You’re adding a “Delete my account” button.**  
Below are the safety steps we’ll build into it (Amber level, because it touches personal data and will delete it).

| Safety part | What we’ll do |
|-------------|---------------|
| **Confirmation** | The button opens a modal that says “This will permanently delete your account and all your data. Are you sure?” and requires a **Yes, delete** click. |
| **Server‑side deletion** | The action calls a secure API route (`/api/delete-account`) that runs on the server with your Supabase service key. No secret keys leak to the browser. |
| **Remove all user data** | The server deletes the user's rows in every table (posts, settings, etc.) *and* any files they uploaded from the Supabase storage bucket. |
| **Anonymise / keep required data** | If you keep, for example, a public‑date‑of‑birth column for analytics, we’ll set it to NULL instead of deleting the row. |
| **Permanent and irreversible** | Once the API completes, there’s no way to recover the data. We’ll show a “Your account has been deleted” page and redirect to the home page. |
| **Two‑step save‑point** | We’ll wrap the change in a small git commit and explain how to restore if something goes wrong. |

 7. Commit a save point, test locally, then push to the deployment.
